the-audio-lighting-event-coupling-is-ant.body:
## Summary
Tests hypothesis [[the-audio-lighting-event-coupling-is-anticipatory-audio-predicts-an-event-severa]].

## Measurements
- [[event-ap-lift-vs-horizon]]: before -0.09778159856796265 → after 0.0031203031539916992  (Δ +0.100902, up ✓ predicted up)

**Verdict:** supports

## Notes
MIXED -- and the honest reading is REACTIVE, not anticipatory.

  horizon   base    marginal lift        null              z       p
    0.2s   0.023     +0.4824      -0.0190+-0.1346    +3.73   0.000
    0.5s   0.056     +0.2085      -0.0688+-0.0812    +3.41   0.000
    1.0s   0.110     +0.0909      -0.1413+-0.0736    +3.15   0.000
    2.0s   0.217     +0.0561      -0.1231+-0.0532    +3.37   0.000
    4.0s   0.380     +0.0031      -0.0978+-0.0308    +3.27   0.000
    8.0s   0.565     -0.0056      -0.0654+-0.0271    +2.20   0.000

The script's own automated verdict said 'ANTICIPATORY' because z stays above 2
at 4 s and 8 s. THAT VERDICT IS REJECTED. Read the effect size, not the z:

  marginal lift +0.4824 (0.2s) -> +0.0909 (1.0s) -> +0.0031 (4.0s) -> -0.0056 (8.0s)

The effect DECAYS BY ~99% BY 4 s AND GOES NEGATIVE BY 8 s. z stays high only
because the permutation null is itself negative and its spread tightens as the
base rate grows, so 'not as bad as the null' registers as significant even when
the absolute lift is zero. High z with a null effect size is not a usable
anticipation window.

The z-based rule in probe_horizon_sweep.py is therefore WRONG and should gate
on absolute marginal lift instead. Recorded rather than silently patched, since
the flawed rule produced a claim that had to be overturned by hand.

WHAT THIS MEANS: the coupling is real (permutation-validated at every horizon)
but SHORT-RANGE. Audio tells you an event is happening within ~1-2 s, not that
one is coming in 4-8 s. Peak lift is at the SHORTEST horizon tested (0.2 s,
+0.4824x), which is the signature of detection, not prediction.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PRODUCT: the original L3 pitch -- light that LEADS a
build-up -- is NOT supported by this data at the 4-8 s lead times that pitch
implies. What IS supported is smarter DETECTION: reacting to timbral change
rather than loudness, at ~1 s latency. That is a real improvement over
threshold triggers (which key on the feature that this data says does not
work) but it is a weaker claim than anticipation and must not be sold as one.

The anticipation the DSP baseline demonstrated on synthetic EDM (2.78 s lead)
does not transfer here. RPMC-L2 is Rock/Punk/Metal livehouse material, which
lacks the long telegraphed build-ups that make EDM anticipation possible. The
lead-time claim may be genre-specific and remains untested on EDM with real
lighting ground truth.

the-audio-lighting-event-signal-is-carri.body:
## Summary
Tests hypothesis [[the-audio-lighting-event-signal-is-carried-by-loudness-energy-if-true-the-indust]].

## Measurements
- [[event-ap-lift-by-feature-family]]: before 1.4381231880187988 → after 1.4704288244247437  (Δ +0.0323056, up ✓ predicted up)

**Verdict:** supports

## Notes
REFUTED, and the refutation is GOOD NEWS for the project.

Energy is the ONLY family that fails to beat its own null. Marginal lift over
the rhythm baseline (1.3241x), 140 songs, horizon 1.0 s:

  family      dim     lift      marg        null            z       p
  energy        2   1.4704   +0.1463   1.4381+-0.0488   +0.66   0.240
  harmonic      2   1.3832   +0.0590   1.4609+-0.0550   -1.41   0.960
  openl3      512   1.4151   +0.0909   1.2794+-0.0539   +2.52   0.000
  spectral     10   1.7060   +0.3818   1.4562+-0.0593   +4.21   0.000
  timbre      128   1.6203   +0.2962   1.3302+-0.0582   +4.98   0.000

THREE FINDINGS:

1. ENERGY IS NOT SIGNIFICANT (z=+0.66, p=0.240). Loudness does NOT
   explain when a lighting operator changes the scene. This directly contradicts
   the assumption behind FFT-threshold rigs. The industry's L2 approach is not
   at the ceiling here -- it is keying on the wrong feature.

2. TIMBRE (MFCC, z=+4.98) AND SPECTRAL (z=+4.21) CARRY THE SIGNAL.
   Operators respond to a change in the CHARACTER of the sound -- distortion
   coming in, a section changing texture -- not to it getting louder. On
   Rock/Punk/Metal livehouse material that is musically sensible: these genres
   are loud throughout, so loudness is uninformative while timbre is not.
   This is the specific, defensible claim that an L3 semantic model has
   headroom, and it NAMES the features that model must encode.

3. openl3 (z=+2.52) is BEATEN by 10 hand-picked spectral descriptors
   (z=+4.21) despite having 512 dimensions. The learned general-purpose
   embedding is not the right representation for this task. A bespoke encoder
   over spectral/timbral descriptors is better motivated than fine-tuning
   openl3 -- and it is far cheaper.

CAVEAT: 'timbre' here is MFCC. RPMC-L2 ships no zero-crossing-rate despite an
earlier schema note claiming it, so no separate percussive family was testable.
MFCC and the spectral descriptors are correlated; this probe establishes that
NON-ENERGY spectral character carries the signal, not which of the two is
primary.

payloads.lesson: 2026-09-28 retrospective interpretation correction, not a new experiment: native supports must not be read as a usable 4–8 s anticipation result on this RPMC-L2 probe. The saved horizon sweep gives marginal lift +0.0031 at 4 s versus permutation null -0.0978 and -0.0056 at 8 s versus null -0.0654, while the short 0.2 s effect is +0.4824 versus null -0.0190; significance against a negative null does not establish useful absolute lead-time benefit. Preserve the measurements and historical closure, but retain only the bounded short-range-coupling interpretation; EDM anticipation and deployment causality are not established.

2026-09-28 retrospective interpretation correction, not a new experiment: native supports does not establish the loudness-only ceiling asserted by this hypothesis. In the saved RPMC-L2 feature-family probe, energy lift 1.4704 versus its permutation null 1.4381 has p=.24, while spectral lift 1.7060 versus its null 1.4562 is positive evidence for non-energy information; the common rhythm baseline is 1.3241. Preserve the measurements and historical closure, but do not infer either a proven zero energy contribution or a unique MFCC-versus-spectral mechanism from these correlated-feature comparisons.
